claim: On Jan 23, 2025 CloudWatch alarms were extended to evaluate metrics data for up to 7 days, a 7x increase from the previous limit of 24 hours.
question: When did CloudWatch alarms start to support evaluating up to 7 days of data, and what was the old limit?

evidence.quote: Posted on: Jan 23, 2025
evidence.heading: Amazon CloudWatch allows alarming on data up to 7 days old

evidence.quote: Amazon CloudWatch now lets customers evaluate metrics data for an extended duration of up to 7 days, a 7x increase from the previous limit of 24 hours.

note: Current truth: cloudwatch-alarm-max-evaluation-period-seven-days (seven days needs a period of at least one hour).

claim: On Apr 2, 2025 CloudWatch Logs raised the maximum log event size to 1 MB, a 4x increase from the previous 256 KB limit.

evidence.quote: Posted on: Apr 2, 2025
evidence.heading: Amazon CloudWatch Logs increases maximum log event size to 1 MB

evidence.quote: Amazon CloudWatch Logs now supports log events up to 1 MB in size, a 4x increase from the previous 256 KB limit.

note: Current truth: cloudwatch-logs-quota-event-size-1024-kb. The CloudTrail 256 KB delivery rule is a different limit.

claim: On May 1, 2025 CloudWatch launched volume tiered pricing for AWS Lambda logs and added Amazon S3 and Amazon Data Firehose as Lambda log delivery destinations.
question: When did CloudWatch add volume tiered pricing for Lambda logs?

evidence.heading: Amazon CloudWatch launches tiered pricing and additional destinations for AWS Lambda logs

evidence.quote: Today, Amazon CloudWatch launched volume tiered pricing for AWS Lambda logs and support for additional delivery destinations.
Additionally, CloudWatch now supports Amazon S3 and Amazon Data Firehose as Lambda log delivery destinations.

note: Current truth: cloudwatch-delivery-class... see the Delivery log class fact cloudwatch-logs-delivery-class-two-days-fixed-retention for the log class used to deliver Lambda logs to S3 or Firehose.

claim: On Sep 17, 2025 CloudWatch launched cross-account and cross-Region log centralization; one copy of the logs is centralized for free and additional copies, including a backup Region, are charged per GB.
question: When did CloudWatch add cross-account cross-Region log centralization, and is the first copy free?

values.display: centralize one copy of logs for free

evidence.quote: Posted on: Sep 17, 2025
evidence.heading: Amazon CloudWatch launches Cross-Account and Cross-Region Log Centralization

evidence.quote: Amazon CloudWatch now offers cross-account and cross-region log centralization, allowing customers to copy log data from multiple AWS accounts and regions into a single destination account.
Customers can centralize one copy of logs for free. Additional copies are charged at $0.05/GB of logs centralized (the backup region feature is considered an additional copy).

evidence.heading: Amazon CloudWatch Composite Alarms adds threshold-based alerting

evidence.quote: To create a threshold-based condition in a composite alarm, simply use the AT_LEAST function in the alarm’s condition.
